summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive web platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx astronomical observations easier to discover, visualize, and compare over time.

Users can search the sky using celestial coordinates, explore observations through interactive 2D and 3D visualizations, inspect astronomical image previews, and navigate between observation dates using a temporal viewer.

Our system combines a React-based interface with a Python/FastAPI backend and scientific processing tools. It supports FITS image inspection, celestial coordinate validation (WCS), image alignment, and quality assessment. The platform also evaluates observational compatibility and clearly distinguishes authentic astronomical data from simulated demonstration content.

We validated key processing capabilities using real SPHEREx FITS observations while documenting the scientific limitations of photometric comparisons.

By transforming complex infrared astronomical data into an accessible visual experience, SPHEREx Explorer helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts investigate the changing sky, understand observations across time, and explore NASA's scientific data responsibly.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer — Project Details

What is SPHEREx Explorer?

SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive astronomical visualization platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx observations easier to access, understand, and explore. Our project transforms complex astronomical datasets into a web-based experience where users can explore the sky, examine observations from different dates, and better understand how infrared astronomical data is collected and analyzed.

How does it work?

Users enter celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) and a search radius to explore a region of the sky. The application presents available observations, their metadata, and image previews through an interactive interface.

The platform combines a 2D celestial map, a 3D sky visualization, observation filters, and a temporal viewer that allows users to move between different observation dates. It also provides tools for comparing observations and examining their scientific characteristics.

Our scientific processing module supports FITS inspection, astronomical coordinate validation through World Coordinate Systems (WCS), image reprojection, visualization, and data-quality assessment.

We tested these capabilities using authentic SPHEREx observations obtained from NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). The application distinguishes verified astronomical observations from simulated demonstration data.

Technologies and development

SPHEREx Explorer uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, and Aladin Lite for its interactive frontend. Its backend is developed with Python and FastAPI, while scientific processing relies on AstroPy, NumPy, reproject, and related astronomical tools.

The system incorporates access to SPHEREx archival resources and was developed using GitHub for collaborative version control and automated testing.

Innovation and benefits

Our innovation lies in combining astronomical data discovery, interactive sky visualization, temporal exploration, and scientific image processing into a single accessible platform.

Rather than requiring users to work directly with complex FITS files or specialized scientific software, SPHEREx Explorer provides an intuitive environment for students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers.

The platform encourages scientific curiosity, improves access to NASA's astronomical resources, and provides a foundation for future studies involving repeated observations of the sky.

Scientific responsibility

Our team prioritized data integrity, astronomical coordinate accuracy, transparency about data provenance, and the distinction between visual comparisons and scientifically validated measurements.

Although SPHEREx Explorer supports the exploration and comparison of observations collected at different times, we do not claim confirmed detections of variable astronomical objects. Advanced photometric comparisons remain subject to additional scientific validation.

Expected impact

We envision SPHEREx Explorer as an educational and exploratory tool that helps make space science more understandable and accessible. By connecting real NASA data with modern interactive technology, our project aims to inspire people to investigate the universe and engage with astronomical research.
